label: copy-phase input digit 3 (fed-back 3, from recall step 2 on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is the digit 3 (100% of activation mass is on in_tok==3, phase 2). Never fires on 3 in the original phase or at the delimiter, and never on any other token. Weak or absent when the 3 is input at recall_idx 1 (i.e. the 3 was the first original token); strongest at recall_idx 2, i.e. when 3 was the second original token, with top examples like 0 3 x n <DEL> 0 [3]. Rate is higher in sequences with more digits. About 28% of copy-phase 3 inputs at recall_idx>=2 are still inactive (precision ~0.72); a to_go cap only adds marginal gains. A second 3 right after another 3 activates more weakly.

issues: The core predicate holds up. On test it scores P 0.725 / R 0.976 / F1 0.832 / mass recall 0.99, matching the report. All activation is in the copy phase on in_tok==3, and none is in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other token.

One claim is misleading: 'firing rate rises with the number of digits'. Per copy-phase 3 (recall_idx>=2), precision actually falls slightly as digits increase: 0.743 with n_digits==1 vs 0.693 with n_digits>=3. The rise in the profile only appears because sequences with more digits contain more 3s.

The explanation leaves out the biggest pattern in the false positives, which is sequence length. Precision is 0.976 for L<=5 but 0.619 for L>=8. At L=4 it is 1.0 for every to_go, at L=6 it is 0.73-0.88, and at L=9 it is 0.60-0.71. The ~28% of 3s that stay inactive are mostly in long sequences, so they are not scattered noise.

No context variable explains the inactive 3s within long sequences. Checked: prev_tok digit/letter (0.69/0.63), out_tok digit/letter (0.72/0.62), next_out, n_seen(DIGITS), and seen(0/1/2/n/x), all landing in the 0.62-0.70 range. Activation looks like it weakens gradually with length and drops below threshold, so I could not find a cleaner predicate. Capping to_go<=5 gives test F1 0.835 vs 0.832, and L<=8 gives 0.762.

The smaller claims check out. recall_idx==1 is weak (precision 0.087, mass 1.1%). A 3 right after another 3 has lower precision (0.58). The firing rate at recall_idx 3 (0.028) is a bit higher than at idx 2 (0.023), though idx 2 has the most activation mass and the top examples. Test misses are 1335 steps holding 1.0% of mass, mostly 3 as the first original token (recall_idx 1).
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input digit 3 (fed-back 3, from recall step 2 on); fires reliably in short sequences, weaker and less reliably as L grows
